blocks.content: An earthquake is the sudden release of stored elastic strain energy accumulated along a fault zone.

rows: Fracture, rupture, and snap-back to relaxed state
Stored energy converted to kinetic seismic waves

items: UPSC Prelims/Mains Focus: Harry Fielding Reid is directly associated with the Elastic Rebound Theory.
Distinction: Strain accumulation is a slow, long-term process, whereas strain release via elastic rebound is rapid and seismic.
Exam Trap: The theory applies specifically to shallow tectonic earthquakes driven by brittle rock failure.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Formulated by Harry Fielding Reid after studying the 1906 San Francisco earthquake along the San Andreas Fault.
Explains that continuous tectonic forces apply slow elastic strain deformation to rocks along a fault line.
When stored stress exceeds the frictional strength of the rock, sudden rupture occurs along the weak zone.
Post-rupture, the snapped rocks spring back into an unstrained shape, releasing stored energy as seismic waves.
